court: The European Court of Human Rights (Second Section)

facts.text: The applicants were the main shareholders of Demirbank, established in 1953.

anchor.surface_text: 3.  The applicants were the main shareholders of Demirbank, established in 1953. In 1999 Demirbank was ranked the fifth largest private bank in Turkey, with 193 branches and 3,885 employees.

facts.text: In 1999 Demirbank was ranked the fifth largest private bank in Turkey, with 193 branches and 3,885 employees.

anchor.surface_text: 3.  The applicants were the main shareholders of Demirbank, established in 1953. In 1999 Demirbank was ranked the fifth largest private bank in Turkey, with 193 branches and 3,885 employees.

facts.text: By a decision dated 6 December 2000 (no. 123), the Banking Regulation and Supervision Board decided to transfer the management and control of Demirbank to the Savings Deposit Insurance Fund.

anchor.surface_text: 4.  By a decision dated 6 December 2000 (no. 123), the Banking Regulation and Supervision Board (Bankalar Düzenleme ve Denetleme Kurulu – hereinafter referred to as “the Board”) decided to transfer the management and control of Demirbank to the Savings Deposit Insurance Fund (Tassarruf Mevduat Sigorta Fonu – hereinafter “the Fund”), pursuant to section 14 (3) of the Banking Activities Act (Law no. 4389).

facts.text: The Board held that Demirbank's assets were insufficient to cover its liabilities and that continuation of its activities would threaten financial system stability.

anchor.surface_text: In its decision, the Board held that the assets of Demirbank were insufficient to cover its liabilities and that the continuation of its activities would threaten the security and stability of the financial system.

facts.text: Demirbank's management and control, and shareholders' privileges except dividends, were transferred to the Fund, which also confiscated all properties belonging to Demirbank.

anchor.surface_text: Accordingly, Demirbank’s management and control, and the privileges of its shareholders except for dividends, were transferred to the Fund. The Fund also confiscated all properties belonging to Demirbank.

facts.text: On 2 February 2001, the applicant company brought administrative proceedings against the Banking Regulation and Supervision Agency before the Ankara Administrative Court seeking annulment of the 6 December 2000 decision.

anchor.surface_text: 5.  On 2 February 2001, the applicant company brought administrative proceedings against the Banking Regulation and Supervision Agency (Bankalar Düzenleme ve Denetleme Kurumu – hereinafter referred to as “the Agency”) before the Ankara Administrative Court, seeking the annulment of the decision of 6 December 2000 regarding the transfer of Demirbank to the Fund.

facts.text: The Ankara Administrative Court found it lacked jurisdiction and transferred the case to the Supreme Administrative Court.

anchor.surface_text: 6.  The Ankara Administrative Court found that it lacked jurisdiction and transferred the case to the Supreme Administrative Court.

facts.text: The applicant company claimed before the Supreme Administrative Court that its property rights had been violated and raised a plea of unconstitutionality under section 14 of the Banking Activities Act.

anchor.surface_text: 7.  In its submissions before the Supreme Administrative Court, the applicant company claimed that its property rights had been violated. It also raised a plea of unconstitutionality under section 14 of the Banking Activities Act.

facts.text: The applicant company stated that prior to November 2000, Demirbank had never encountered major financial problems and that no warning had been given as required by section 14(2) of the Act.

anchor.surface_text: The applicant company further stated that prior to November 2000, Demirbank had never encountered major financial problems. It was pointed out that pursuant to section 14 (2) of the Act, a bank with financial difficulties should first be given a warning to strengthen its financial structure and be allowed time to take specific measures. However, no such warning had been given in the instant case.

facts.text: The Board had not claimed that Demirbank’s financial situation was so weak that it could not be strengthened even if specific measures were taken.

anchor.surface_text: Secondly, the Board had not claimed that Demirbank’s financial situation was so weak that it could not be strengthened even if specific measures were taken.

facts.text: Following the transfer of the bank to the Fund, a General Assembly composed of the Fund’s officials exonerated the former managers of Demirbank, holding they had not been at fault.

anchor.surface_text: Lastly, the applicant company stated that following the transfer of the bank to the Fund, a General Assembly composed of the Fund’s officials had exonerated the former managers of Demirbank, holding that they had not been at fault in the incident leading to the bank’s transfer.

facts.text: On 3 June 2003 the Supreme Administrative Court dismissed the case, holding the takeover was in accordance with section 14(3) of the Banking Activities Act.

anchor.surface_text: 8.  After examining the file, on 3 June 2003 the Supreme Administrative Court dismissed the case. It held that the takeover of the bank by the Fund had been in accordance with section 14 (3) of the Banking Activities Act.

facts.text: The applicant company lodged an appeal against the Supreme Administrative Court's dismissal.

anchor.surface_text: The applicant company lodged an appeal.

facts.text: On 18 December 2003 the Joint Administrative Chambers of the Supreme Administrative Court quashed the 3 June 2003 decision, holding the Board should have objectively evaluated the bank’s financial situation before ordering the transfer.

anchor.surface_text: 9.  On 18 December 2003 the Joint Administrative Chambers of the Supreme Administrative Court decided to quash the decision of 3 June 2003. In its judgment, the court held that prior to ordering the transfer of Demirbank to the Fund, the Board should have carried out an objective evaluation of the bank’s financial situation.

facts.text: The Board should have ordered Demirbank to take specific measures under section 14(2) before applying section 14(3).

anchor.surface_text: The court also concluded that the Board should first have ordered Demirbank to take specific measures in accordance with section 14 (2) of the Banking Activities Act before applying section 14 (3) of the Act.

facts.text: On 5 November 2004 the Supreme Administrative Court upheld the Joint Chambers' decision, annulling the Board’s decision of 6 December 2000 to take over Demirbank by the Fund.

anchor.surface_text: 11.  On 5 November 2004, the Supreme Administrative Court upheld the decision of the Joint Administrative Chambers of the Supreme Administrative Court. In its decision the Supreme Administrative Court held that: ... the Banking Regulation and Supervision Board’s decision of 6 December 2000 ordering the takeover of Demirbank by the Fund is unanimously annulled.

facts.text: The Agency's further appeal and request for rectification were rejected on 14 April 2005 and 15 December 2005 respectively; the final decision was served on 13 March 2006.

anchor.surface_text: 12.  A further appeal and a request for rectification lodged by the Agency were rejected on 14 April 2005 and 15 December 2005 respectively. The final decision was served on the applicant company’s representative on 13 March 2006.

facts.text: On 20 September 2001 the Fund sold Demirbank to HSBC bank for 350,000,000 US Dollars.

anchor.surface_text: 13. In the meantime, while the proceedings against the Agency were still pending, on 20 September 2001 the Fund entered into an agreement with the HSBC bank, and sold Demirbank to the latter for 350,000,000 US Dollars.

facts.text: On 20 September 2001 the second applicant brought administrative proceedings against the Fund seeking annulment of the agreement to sell Demirbank to HSBC.

anchor.surface_text: 14.  On 20 September 2001 the second applicant brought administrative proceedings against the Fund in the Ankara Administrative Court, seeking the annulment of the agreement to sell Demirbank to HSBC.

facts.text: On 21 April 2004 the Ankara Administrative Court annulled the agreement between the Fund and HSBC, holding the sale unlawful following the Supreme Administrative Court's annulment of the transfer of Demirbank to the Fund.

anchor.surface_text: 15.  Given that the transfer of Demirbank to the Fund had been found to be unlawful by the Joint Administrative Chambers of the Supreme Administrative Court, on 21 April 2004 the Ankara Administrative Court annulled the agreement entered into by the Fund and HSBC on 20 September 2001. In its decision the Ankara Administrative Court held that: ... the subsequent sale of Demirbank to HSBC Bank has also become unlawful and the decision that is the subject of these proceedings is therefore unlawful. This act is therefore declared null and void.

facts.text: An appeal and request for rectification by the Fund were rejected on 3 June 2005 and 24 February 2006 respectively.

anchor.surface_text: 16.  An appeal and a request for rectification lodged by the Fund were rejected on 3 June 2005 and 24 February 2006 respectively.

facts.text: On 11 May 2006 the second applicant requested the Agency to comply with and enforce the Supreme Administrative Court’s judgments, requesting restitutio in integrum by returning Demirbank to its previous owners.

anchor.surface_text: 17.  On 11 May 2006 the second applicant requested the Agency to comply with the Supreme Administrative Court’s judgments and to enforce them. Relying on the restitutio in integrum principle, she requested that Demirbank be returned to its previous owners.

facts.text: On 10 July 2006 the Agency informed the second applicant that enforcement was impossible as Demirbank had been struck off the commercial register following its sale to HSBC.

anchor.surface_text: 18.  On 10 July 2006 the Agency informed the second applicant that it would be impossible to enforce the judgments as, following its sale to HSBC, Demirbank had been struck off the commercial register.
